messages:
maria: heads up — seeing a recurring decode-batching fragmentation and p95 regression tied to function-invoke pauses + structured output (json with stop tokens). started ~03:40 UTC on canary cluster.

dan: can you paste the profiler traces or an example request/trace? :eyes:

maria: here's a short trace from one offending request (simplified):

```
Batcher: formed batch_size=1 (expected >8)
Reason: fn-invoke; waiting for external tool response
KV cache: session=abc123 hit_rate=0.52 (baseline 0.86)
Kernel: picked=attn_short_seq_cuda_v2
Decode: stop_token emitted during tool-handoff -> fragment flush
Latency: p50=95ms p95=380ms (baseline p95~120ms)
```

maria: note: these sessions are normally long-context chat; toolcall returns structured JSON and includes its own stop tokens which seem to interact badly with our stop-detection and batch completion.

kevin: hmm — two things jump out: (1) kernel selection expects contiguous decode without long pauses; some kernels hold different buffering behavior for kv cache and stream flush. (2) stop-token detection currently coerces a batch flush on first stop-match which collapses other concurrent requests into tiny batches if they hit toolcall boundaries at different offsets.

lina: proposed quick workaround: treat toolcall-parked requests as "parked" and keep them out of the main batch formation until they resume OR let them participate in prefix-only batching (no decode tokens counted toward token_budget_target while parked). pseudocode: 

```
if request.state == PARKED:
  allow_prefix_cache_updates()
  exclude_from_decode_budget()
else:
  include_in_batch()
```

lina: this should preserve larger batch shapes for active decodes and avoid tiny one-offs.

ashok: +1. we also saw kv cache hit-rate drop because we invalidate session-level KV on early stop-flushes. if we can avoid unconditional cache eviction on toolcall stop tokens that should help.

dan: timeline: can we try two small experiments on canary: (A) mark parked requests excluded from token_budget accounting (token_budget_target remains 32 globally) (B) change kernel selection heuristic to prefer "preemptible" kernel for sequences likely to hit toolcalls (fast context switch friendly) and compare.

kevin: I instrumented kernel costs — preemptible kernel has slightly higher per-token cost but much lower tail latency when we preempt/resume. sample numbers from local bench (ctx=2048):

```
kernel=attn_default: throughput=1200 tok/s cost_factor=1.0 p95=110ms
kernel=attn_preempt: throughput=1050 tok/s cost_factor=1.08 p95=70ms under preempt patterns
```

kevin: switching to attn_preempt for suspect sessions seems promising.

maria: rolled config A on canary at 04:05 UTC (exclude parked from token_budget). initial signals: batch size median went from 4->9, p95 dropped ~25%. KV hit_rate improved from 0.52 -> 0.74.

perf-bot: [04:12 UTC] Canary metric note — decode_batch_mean_size up 2.1x, p95_latency down 28% (canary cluster id: rwd-canary-3).

dan: nice. canary B (kernel switch) results?

kevin: rolled B shortly after. early numbers look good for tails; overall cost increased ~4% but per-request latency volatile cases improved ~45% at p95.

lina: we should still address stop-token logic — right now any stop token triggers immediate batch commit. suggestion: add a short debounce window (2–4ms) before committing a batch on stop detection to allow other peers to catch up. combined with parked-exclusion this might be best.

ashok: agree. also change cache eviction: only evict session KV if request completes and kv_age > threshold OR explicit cache-invalid flag from model. avoids losing context when a stop token comes from tool-structured output.

maria: plan: 1) ship parked-exclusion config to prod for dedicated clusters behind feature flag, 2) enable kernel preempt heuristic for sessions with toolcall probability > 0.2, 3) implement stop-debounce (2ms) + KV eviction gating. target: 48h rollout with metrics guardrails.

kevin: I'll open kernel chooser PR with tests and perf bench results. filename: runtime/kernel-chooser/preemptable-heuristic.

lina: I'll send the batcher patch for parked-exclusion and stop-debounce. small unit tests included for batch shape invariants.

dan: ops: can we add a temporary alert for decode_batch_median_size < 3 on prod so we catch regressions during rollout?

perf-bot: [04:48 UTC] Alert rule created by dan: decode_batch_median_size_low (threshold=3) — notify #eng-oncall.

maria: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short postmortem once prod rollout is stable. spikes felt worse on some workload slices (agents that call tools frequently) so we'll add per-model tagging to route them to preempt kernels by default. :thumbsup:

kevin: FYI I saw a weird edge where structured outputs that include explicit newline sequences triggered our stop regex earlier — I'll add a more conservative stop-detection whitelist for toolcall contexts.

ashok: added a small repro harness in infra (link removed) that simulates alternating tool waits and structured stop tokens; using it to validate the patches.

maria: OK wrapping up — action owners: kevin (kernel heuristic PR), lina (batcher patch), dan (alerts + rollout plan), ashok (repro + kv eviction patch). I'll coordinate canary -> prod over next 48h.

lina: noted. will ping updates here. :rocket:
